record.original_question: Does every metric on S^2 admit a stationary Θ-graph?

evidence.quote: Does every metric on S^2 admit a stationary Θ-graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Θ-graph (theta-graph) is a finite graph consisting of two vertices joined by three edges. Given a smooth Riemannian metric g on the 2-sphere S², a stationary Θ-graph (or stationary Θ-net) on (S², g) is a continuous map from a Θ-graph into S² such that:
(i) each of the three edges is mapped to a (non-constant) geodesic arc with respect to g connecting the two image vertices, and
(ii) at each of the two vertices, the sum of the unit tangent vectors of the three incident geodesic arcs (pointing outward from that vertex) equals zero.

Equivalently, the configuration is a critical point of the length functional on the space of maps from a Θ-graph into S².

Question: Does every smooth Riemannian metric g on S² admit a stationary Θ-graph?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, going back to Hass–Morgan (1996), remains open. While general existence results for stationary geodesic nets on closed manifolds (Nabutovsky–Rotman) and generic-density results (Liokumovich–Staffa, 2025) are known, no proof has been given that every Riemannian metric on S² admits a stationary Θ-graph specifically.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets on the 2-sphere — Hass and Morgan
status_evidence.snippet: Studies geodesic nets on S² and raises the question of stationary Θ-nets for arbitrary metrics.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a stationary Θ-graph for every metric on S² is posed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Generic density of stationary geodesic nets that are not closed geodesics
status_evidence.snippet: For a generic Riemannian metric, stationary geodesic nets are dense; the existence problem for specific net topologies (e.g. Θ-graphs) on every metric remains.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work establishes generic density but does not resolve existence of stationary Θ-graphs for every metric on S².
